Monthly vs. Annual Subscription Difference
Annual savings calculation and how switching between the two works.
You can subscribe to Ziadah on a monthly or annual basis. Both give you the same features, but the annual subscription saves you a noticeable amount.
Annual Subscription Savings
The annual subscription offers a discount equivalent to two free months compared to monthly payments. In other words, you pay for 10 months and get a full 12 months.
When to Choose Monthly?
If you're in a trial period and not sure about continuing
If your store activity is seasonal (Ramadan, holidays)
If you're trying Ziadah for the first time
When to Choose Annual?
If you're confident about continuing after the first month
If your store is active year-round
If you want to reduce the administrative burden of monthly renewals
Switching from Monthly to Annual

You can upgrade to the annual subscription at any time from the dashboard. The remaining balance from your monthly subscription is automatically calculated and deducted from the annual subscription cost.
Switching from Annual to Monthly
You can switch to a monthly subscription when your current year ends. You cannot switch to monthly during the annual subscription period before it expires, but you can stop automatic renewal.

Technical & Integration
How Does Ziadah Integrate with Zid, Salla and Shopify?
Explanation of the technical connection between Ziadah and both platforms and how sync works.
Ziadah integrates with the Zid, Salla and Shopify platforms through official, certified APIs. This deep integration is what makes recommendations accurate and instant.
Technical Connection Mechanism

When you install Ziadah, it receives an OAuth token — a secure access key that allows it to read product and order data without needing your password. This key is encrypted and can be revoked at any time.
Continuous Sync
Products: Instant sync when a product is added or modified
Inventory: Updated every 15 minutes
Orders: Instant sync with every new order
Categories: Synced on any change
Managing Granted Permissions
At any time, you can review the permissions granted to Ziadah from your Zid, Salla or Shopify dashboard, in the Apps section. Permissions are read-only — Ziadah cannot modify your store's data.
Performance and Speed
The integration system is built with Edge Computing — our servers are located in regions close to Saudi Arabia to ensure a response time of less than 100 milliseconds in most cases.
If you notice a delay in product changes appearing in Ziadah's recommendations, you can perform a "Manual Sync" from the Ziadah dashboard in the Settings section.

Troubleshooting Common Issues
List of the most common problems and how to solve them yourself.
We've compiled the 8 most common technical issues merchants face, along with quick solutions you can apply yourself in minutes.
Issue 1: Recommendations Don't Appear in the Store
Ensure the campaign is set to "Active" and not "Paused"
Ensure the theme supports Ziadah or that the code has been manually embedded

Issue 4: Number of Influenced Orders Is Very Low

Ensure you're viewing the correct time period

Creating & Managing Widgets
How to create a new widget, customize it, and publish it to your store step by step.
Widgets are the heart of Ziadah. Each one is a smart element that appears in your store at the right moment and suggests the products or offers that raise the value of the order.
The widget types
Buy More Save More - tiered discounts by quantity
Buy Together - products that complete each other at a combined price
Add-ons - small optional extras beside the main product

Creating a widget
In the sidebar, open "Widgets" and click "+ New widget"

Buy More Save More Widget
How to set up tiered quantity discounts to increase average order value.
The Buy More Save More widget shows the shopper a plain table: buy 2 for 10% off, 3 for 15%, 5 for 25%. It lifts the average quantity per order by 30-45%.
Setting the discount tiers
Pick Buy More Save More from the widget list
Click "+ Add tier" to add a new band
For each band set the minimum quantity and the discount, as a percentage or a fixed amount
Up to five tiers are available on Growth and above
Set the widget heading and the nudge line, something like "Save more when you buy more"
Choose the page: product or category
Hit "Publish"
Advanced settings
Apply to specific products, a whole category, or the entire store
Set an end date for the offer, which is useful for a season
Hide the discount on the product card and show it only inside the widget
Turn on the "stock left" counter to create urgency
Tiered discounts work well on consumables: perfume, personal care, food. Start with three tiers. More than that tends to stall the decision.
Buy Them All Bundle
How to build a fixed set of products that is added to the cart in one click at one price.

Buy Them All is a bundle type. You pick a fixed set of products, and the shopper sees it in one window at one price and adds all of it with the Add all to cart button. The products are locked inside the set, so the shopper cannot remove one.
Setting it up, step by step
From the side menu choose Campaigns, then Create New
In the Campaign Goal step choose Buy them all, then Next Step
In Bundle Structure write the widget title and subtitle, then add the products in the set with Add products and set the quantity of each
In Rewards pick one type: a fixed bundle price, a percentage off, a fixed amount off, a free gift only, or cashback, then fill in its fields
In Campaign Rules set the event that shows the set, such as viewing a product page, and the products it appears on: specific products, all products, or cart value
In Content & Style enter the campaign title and the start and end dates, and set the product appearance, the action buttons and the window style (overlay or embedded)
Click Publish Campaign
Reward types and their settings
You pick one type per campaign, and gifts and free shipping can be added on top.
Fixed bundle price: you enter the price of the whole set, and you see the sum of the products on their own and what the shopper saves

Percentage off: the discount percentage and an optional maximum discount, applied to the whole bundle, the cheapest item, or each item separately, rounded down to the nearest riyal, with a percent badge on the cards
Fixed amount off: a riyal amount applied once per bundle or on every item, or split across the items by price
Free gift only: no discount; you choose the gift products and the maximum quantity of each, and the shopper picks one gift or several, or gets them all

Cashback: a fixed amount or a percentage of the bundle that goes back to the shopper's wallet, with an optional maximum and an optional minimum bundle value, credited after payment, after delivery or after the return window, and an expiry in days
The event: viewing a product page, the homepage or a category, adding to the cart, viewing the cart, removing an item from it, starting checkout, or placing an order
The products: specific products, all products, or cart value, and the presentation: products only or products plus a coupon
The style: overlay or embedded, with the window shape and the products shape (horizontal sliding, vertical sliding or grid) set separately for mobile and desktop
On the product page: above Add to cart, below the description, or in a tab
After adding: stay on the page, redirect to checkout, or redirect to the cart
A window that shows the products in the set at one price, next to what they cost separately
An Add all to cart button that adds every product in one click
The products are fixed inside the set and cannot be removed from it
Choose products that naturally sell together, such as a complete kit, so the set makes sense to the shopper. Check the live preview at each step before you publish.
Buy Together Widget
Suggest complementary products together at a bundled price and increase average cart value.
The Buy Together widget puts two or three products in one place with a single "Add all to cart" button. The AI picks the combination from what shoppers actually buy together.
Setting it up
Pick the Buy Together widget
Choose the mode: automatic (AI) or manual
On automatic, the AI picks the best combination itself
On manual, choose the products you want tied together, two to four of them
Decide whether the set carries a discount, and how much
Set the block heading, something like "Frequently bought together"
Choose where it appears: the product page
Getting good results
Pick products that work together: shoes and socks, a device and its charger, perfume and body lotion
A discount between 5% and 15% converts best
Avoid pairing across a big price gap, a 10 SAR item next to a 500 SAR one
Use good photography. The widget shows the images prominently
After a week on automatic, check Analytics to see which combination converted best. You can then pin it manually for your top sellers.
Add-ons Widget
Add small optional extras beside the main product for customers to select with one click.

The Add-ons widget puts a short list of checkboxes next to the add-to-cart button. The idea comes from the drive-through: "do you want fries with that?" It is simple enough that the shopper does not have to think about it.
What add-ons look like in practice
Appliances: an extended warranty, a carry case, a spare charger
Fashion: name embroidery, premium gift wrap
Perfume: a matching body splash, the gift set box
Electronics: home installation, a protective case, a screen protector
Pick the Add-ons widget and choose the product or category it applies to
Click "+ Add option" and give it a name and a price
Choose the pricing: a fixed amount, or a percentage of the product price
Drag the options into order, most wanted at the top
Decide whether the shopper can pick more than one
Keep it to four or five options. The fewer the choices, the higher the take-up. An add-on under 15% of the product price is accepted far more often.
Related Products Widget
Display similar or same-category products to guide customers toward more discovery.
The Related Products widget sits at the bottom of the product page or in the sidebar and shows similar products by category, by tag, or by what other shoppers looked at after this one.
Modes
Automatic (AI): reads browsing behaviour and picks what fits each shopper
By category: products from the same category
By tag: products that share particular tags
Manual: you choose what to link
Layout
A horizontal scroll strip, which suits the bottom of a product page
A grid, which suits the home page or a category page
Between 3 and 12 products
Hide out-of-stock products automatically
Show a "best seller" badge on your standout products
Filter by price range, for instance never show something more than twice the price of the current product
The automatic mode gets better once it has data, usually around 200 visits. Start on "by category" and move to automatic later.
Bundle Deals Widget
Create a product bundle at a special price and present it as one ready-to-buy unit.
A bundle differs from Buy Together in that it is one fixed package at one combined price. The AI presents it as its own clear card rather than as a list of suggestions.
When to use a bundle
To clear particular stock quickly
For a season or a holiday: a Mother's Day bundle, a Ramadan bundle
To launch a new product alongside one that already sells
To lift the average order value inside one category
Creating one
Open "Bundle Deals" and click "+ New bundle"
Name it, something like "The complete travel kit"
Add between two and six products
Set the total price. The saving is calculated for you
Choose a cover image, or let the system assemble one from the product photos
Choose where it appears and which products trigger it
State the saving plainly, "Save 45 SAR" or "20% off". A bundle that saves more than 15% is added to the cart at roughly twice the rate of one that saves less.
Cross-Sell Widget
Suggest complementary products on the cart page to increase order value before checkout.

The Cross-Sell widget appears on the cart or checkout page and suggests products that complete what is already in the cart. It is one of the best moments to suggest anything, because the shopper has already decided to buy.
How it differs from the other widgets
Buy Together appears on the product page, before anything is in the cart
Cross-Sell appears in the cart or at checkout, after the decision to buy
Cross-Sell converts better because of that timing
Pick the Cross-Sell widget
Choose where it appears: cart, checkout, or both
Choose the mode: automatic (AI) or manual rules
On manual rules, write them as "if product X is in the cart, suggest Y"
Set a price ceiling for what may be suggested, so nothing costs more than the cart
What you cross-sell should be cheaper than the average of what is already in the cart. A 20 SAR suggestion against a 200 SAR cart is added about 40% more often than a 150 SAR one.
Smart Coupon Widget
Create a discount coupon that activates automatically on a cart condition to encourage checkout.
The smart coupon widget shows a nudge with a progress bar, so the shopper can see how far they are from the discount. For example: "Add 30 SAR and get 15% off."
Coupon types
A fixed amount: "Get 20 SAR off an order of 150 SAR"
A percentage: "Get 15% off an order of 200 SAR"
Free shipping: "Add 50 SAR to the cart for free shipping"
A free gift: a product added free above a set spend
Pick the coupon widget
Choose the incentive: discount, free shipping or gift
Set the cart minimum that unlocks it
Set the discount amount, or pick the gift product
Write the nudge, something like "You are one step from your discount"
Turn on the progress bar so the remaining distance is visible
Choose where it appears: the top of the cart, or a fixed bar across every page
The progress bar lifts add-to-cart by 25-35%, for the same reason a loyalty punch card works: people finish what they have started.

Customer Targeting & Personalization

Growth Strategies
Best Strategies for Fashion Stores
Set bundles, accessory grouping, and tiered discounts — a fashion guide.

Fashion stores have a golden opportunity with Ziadah because products are naturally interconnected — complete outfits, complementary accessories, and different sizes are all opportunities for additional sales.
Strategy 1: Complete the Look Bundle
The strongest strategy for fashion stores. When a customer views a clothing item, suggest the complete outfit. The increase in cart value is typically 40–70%.
Classify your products correctly: shirt, pants, shoes, bag
Use shared tags for coordinating items (e.g., "classic beige")
Create a campaign with the "Increase Cart Value" goal on the product page
Choose the "Combo" display method with an image of the complete outfit
Strategy 2: Accessory Grouping
Accessories (belt, watch, glasses) are added at a relatively low price but achieve a significant increase in cart value.
Use Add-ons on the product page to display low-priced accessories
The add-on price should not exceed 25% of the main product price
Use clear images of the accessory with the main product
Strategy 3: Alternative Sizes and Colors
If the desired size is unavailable, suggest an available alternative of the same design in a different color or a similar size. This reduces store abandonment without a purchase.
Performance Indicators for Fashion Stores
Average cart value: Goal to increase by 30–50% within 3 months
Accessory purchase rate with a main item: Goal of 20–30%
Suggested product viewing rate: Goal of 40% or higher
During fashion season (Ramadan, September back-to-school, and holidays), activate special complete outfit campaigns with limited discounts for 72 hours only.
Boosting Sales for Food & Beverage Stores
Combo strategies and subscription models for food and beverage stores.
Food and beverage stores have a naturally high repeat purchase rate — the challenge is increasing each order's value and converting random buyers into regular subscribers.
Strategy 1: Combo Meals and Bundles
Combining complementary products (drink + meal + dessert) in a bundle at a better price than individual purchases. This increases order value and saves the customer time.
Study the most popular product combinations customers already buy together
Create an official bundle at 10–15% less than buying individually
Display it on the product page and cart page
Strategy 2: Larger Quantities at Better Prices
For recurring consumable products (coffee, tea, nuts), suggest a larger size or greater quantity with a tiered discount.
Use the "Buy More Save More" display method
Example: "1 kg for 50 SAR, or 3 kg for 130 SAR"
This increases cart value and reduces purchase frequency benefiting both you and the customer
Strategy 3: Order Completion
When a customer adds a product to their cart, suggest a product that naturally complements it.
Coffee → Add sugar, milk, or biscuits
Tea → Add honey or dried thyme
Nuts → Add dried berries or chocolate
Strategy 4: Recurring Subscriptions
For products that are purchased regularly, suggest a monthly subscription option with a fixed discount. This transforms random purchases into regular recurring revenue.
Start with the "Order Completion" strategy as it's the simplest and fastest-yielding for food and beverage stores. Apply it on the cart page and you'll notice a difference within a week.
Maximizing Profits for Beauty & Care Stores
Complete care routines and complementary product recommendations to grow the beauty cart.

Beauty and care stores have a unique advantage: their customers are looking for a complete routine, not just a single product. The right strategies turn this search into a significant cart value increase opportunity.
Strategy 1: Complete Care Routine
The strongest strategy in beauty. When a customer views a moisturizing cream, suggest the facial cleanser, serum, and sunscreen as a "complete routine."
Classify your products into routine steps: cleansing, preparation, treatment, moisturizing, protection
Create shared tags for products that work together
Display the "Complete Routine" as a bundle on each product page
Use success stories and before-and-after photos to convince the customer
Strategy 2: Skin Type Complements
If a customer buys a product for oily skin, suggest other products for the same skin type. This personalization increases trust and purchase rates.
Add the suitable skin type in product descriptions
Use tags like "oily_skin," "dry_skin," and "combination_skin"
Create targeting rules based on categories the customer has previously purchased from
Strategy 3: Trial Size and Full Size
Suggest a small trial size first, then on the thank you page suggest the full size at a discount. This builds trust and increases customer lifetime value.
Performance Indicators for Beauty Stores
Average products per cart: Goal of 3+ products per order
Repeat customer rate: Goal of 40% of orders
Complete routine purchase rate: Goal of 15–25%
Ramadan season is the highest-selling period for beauty stores in Saudi Arabia. Prepare "Ramadan Routine" bundles 4 weeks before the holy month and activate campaigns on day one.
Using Data to Improve Campaign Performance
Reading analytics reports and making smart decisions based on data.
Data is the difference between guessing and smart decisions. Learn how to read Ziadah's reports to make decisions that continuously improve your results.
Report 1: Campaign Performance
The most important report to start with weekly. It shows additional revenue, click-through rate, and conversion rate for each campaign.
Look for the campaign with the highest CTR — this campaign should be expanded
Look for the campaign with the highest conversion rate — this one has an excellent user experience
Pause campaigns that don't exceed 0.5% CTR after a full week
Report 2: Most Recommended and Purchased Products
Shows which products are recommended most and which are actually purchased from recommendations. The gap between the two indicates pricing or image issues.
Report 3: Customer Journey
Tracks the complete path from seeing the recommendation to purchasing. If the customer clicks but doesn't buy, the problem is on the product page, not the recommendation.
Data-Driven Decision-Making Framework
Identify one metric you want to improve this week (e.g., CTR)
View the report and identify the weakest campaigns for this metric
Make only one change (e.g., change the display method)
Wait 5 days and monitor the result
If the metric improves, continue. If not, try a different change
Don't change more than one variable at a time. If you change the goal, display method, and suggestion point all at once, you won't know which one made the difference.
Holiday Season Preparation Guide
How to prepare your store and Ziadah for Ramadan, Black Friday, and holidays.
Major seasons represent 30-40% of annual sales for many stores. Proper advance preparation means a significant difference in final numbers.
The most important season for Saudi stores. Successful merchants start preparation 4-6 weeks in advance.
4 weeks before: Review your products and add Ramadan-specific seasonal items
3 weeks before: Create Ramadan bundles (e.g., coffee, dates, and sweets set)
2 weeks before: Activate special Ramadan campaigns at appropriate suggestion points
1 week before: Test all campaigns and verify recommendation accuracy
During Ramadan: Monitor analytics daily and adjust underperforming campaigns
Black Friday & Cyber Monday
A golden opportunity to use smart coupons. Offer discounts that escalate with cart value — the more the customer adds, the bigger the discount.
Cart SAR 200 → 10% off
Cart SAR 400 → 15% off
Cart SAR 600 → 20% off
National Day, Eid Al-Fitr & Eid Al-Adha
These occasions are ideal for gift recommendations as 'complete sets' with premium packaging. Ready-made gift bundles have a much higher conversion rate than individual products.
Create smart seasonal campaigns that activate and deactivate automatically on specific dates. This saves you effort and ensures each season gets its perfectly timed campaign.
Accurately Measuring ROI from Ziadah
Step-by-step method to calculate the exact return on your investment in Ziadah.
Ziadah is an investment, and every investment needs an ROI calculation. This guide gives you a clear formula to accurately calculate ROI and determine whether you're truly benefiting.
ROI Calculation Formula
ROI = ((Additional Revenue - Subscription Cost) / Subscription Cost) × 100
How to Calculate Additional Revenue
Additional revenue is the amount you wouldn't have earned without Ziadah. The dashboard calculates it automatically, but here's how it's computed:
Conservative method: Revenue from recommended products added to cart directly from the recommendation
Comprehensive method: Increase in average cart value multiplied by total number of orders
Precise method: Using A/B testing with a control group that doesn't see recommendations
Practical Example

A store with 300 monthly orders averaging SAR 250 → total SAR 75,000. After Ziadah, the average rose to SAR 320 → total SAR 96,000. Additional revenue = SAR 21,000. If the subscription is SAR 1,000/month, ROI = (21,000 - 1,000) / 1,000 × 100 = 2000%
Indicators of a Successful Store with Ziadah
Positive ROI after 1 month: A healthy sign
ROI above 500% after 3 months: Excellent performance
If ROI is negative after 1 month: Review campaign settings
Don't calculate ROI in the first 2 weeks. Wait at least a full month to get enough data for an accurate assessment of the return.
